one_sentence: Theophysics argues that every physical law has a structurally identical spiritual counterpart, differing only by a free-will term, and that full integration yields mathematical identity between physical and spiritual coherence.
executive_summary: This document presents the complete framework of Theophysics, claiming that the mathematical structure of physical laws—gravity, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, and others—maps exactly onto spiritual realities such as grace, sin, faith, and love. Each law is shown to have a spiritual counterpart with a single asymmetry term representing free will. The framework culminates in a master equation integrating all ten variables, whose equilibrium condition mathematically describes salvation. The document also proves that any foundational ground must be unprovable from within the system it grounds, and that the properties of such a ground match the classical definition of God. The conclusion is that faith and reason are not in conflict; rather, mathematics requires an external, infinite source of grace for any system to achieve lasting coherence.
short_summary: This document is the canonical explanation of the Theophysics framework, presenting ten laws that pair physical equations with spiritual counterparts. The core structural claim is that every physical law has an identical spiritual form differing only by a free-will asymmetry term. Key evidence includes the exact mathematical match between Shannon entropy and the Logos information equation, and the QCD potential matching the love-binding equation. This matters because it provides a mathematical foundation for theological concepts, showing that the structure of reality requires an external, infinite ground—the classical definition of God.
